newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at end on quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate inches up at end on quiet trade.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 25 basis points at 19.00 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said the money market shunned euphoria in the stock and foreign exchange markets on GDP data on a general feeling that primary rates had now reached floor levels.
"After primary rates fell modestly, we just had a quiet day. Even the monthly cut-off didn't shake us," a trader said.
Wednesday saw the cut-off date for banks settling balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.

Traders said ample liquidity allowed banks to clear the obstacle often presented by the cut-off date. This has in the past often led to a last-minute scramble for cash-strapped banks to make payments, and thus sent secondary rates up on the resulting liquidity squeeze.

But the contained drop in rates at Tuesday night's Cetes auction mostly kept the market in check. Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 19.46 percent at its weekly primary auction on Tuesday night.
This was a fall of 23 basis points from last week and the lowest rate since an abrupt devaluation of the peso in December 1994 triggered a financial crisis.
"Demand at the auction was mainly for longer term issues, so it is acknowledged that rates can hardly fall further, or if they do, it will be marginally," another trader said.
"Conditions are still good, but the important thing now is to hold on to investment rather than lure it," he added.
Banco de Mexico drained 2.197 billion pesos from the system by holding four secondary market auctions.
Traders said a strong peso further steadied secondary rates. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 3.45 centavos firmer at 7.7640/7.7665 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 20 basis points at 20.40 percent.
A hefty 9.184 billion pesos of liquidity was scheduled to return to the market on Thursday from prior central bank participation.

Nonetheless, traders said liquidity would be tapped by corporate tax bills estimated at eight billion pesos, and an overplacement of 1.469 billion pesos in paper carried over from the primary auction.
